info.title: PrintFlow API
info.description: Store-scoped print order queue: CSV intake, PSD composition, TIFF/PDF output, CUPS dispatch.

get.description: Liveness: the process is up. Public, so it says nothing about the system.
Readiness: the process is up and can reach its database. Public and minimal.
Admins see every store. Operators see only their own (needed for headers/filters).

schema.title: Response List Formats Print Formats Get

post.description:
Find the baked-in placeholder in a design and return its box.

Lets an admin place the text box by pointing at the placeholder's colour
instead of reading coordinates out of Photoshop.

Report what a box will actually produce, and what a size actually needs.

`font_size` is a ceiling in pixels that the renderer shrinks from, so a
79px-tall box caps the type at 68px however large the format asks for. At
508 dpi that is 9.6pt — nothing like what "68" suggests, which is why the
field reads as broken. `min_box_*` is the half an admin can act on.

post.description:
Render the PSD + text, then deliver it according to `delivery`.

PRINTER dispatches to CUPS from the server. DOWNLOAD marks the order printed
and leaves the operator to print the file locally — the only route that works
when the app runs in the cloud and the printer is attached to the operator's
own machine. PROOF renders the artifacts and leaves the order status alone.

Both PRINTER and DOWNLOAD flip the order to PRINTED and, if it was already
PRINTED, count as a reprint.

get.description: Readable by operators too: the print dialog shows text the way it will print.

FitTextRequest.title: FitTextRequest
FitTextRequest.description:
Ask what size a box would actually produce, and what box a size needs.

`font_size` on a format is a ceiling in *pixels*, not a setting — the
renderer shrinks it until the text fits. Designers think in points, and at
508 dpi a point is 7.06 px, so a 68px cap is 9.6pt: far smaller than the
number suggests. Both halves of that confusion are answered here.
